stories.title: A King's Book of Chess Puzzles
stories.titleCn: 国王的国际象棋谜题书

variants.lucy: More than seven centuries ago, a gentle Spanish king named Alfonso wanted to share his love of play. He had his helpers create a giant, hand-written book filled with board games. Inside its thick pages, artists drew the earliest chess brain-teasers ever recorded in Europe. It even described how each carved figure should glide across the board and what bright shades they should be painted.
variants.luca: Imagine a king from the Middle Ages who wanted to gather all the best games in the world! King Alfonso commanded his writers to make a giant, heavy book. It held the oldest chess strategies ever written down in Europe, showing players how to march their pieces and what colors to paint them for battle.
variants.cn: 七百多年前，西班牙有一位温和的国王，名叫阿方索。他特别喜欢玩游戏，还想把这份快乐分享给所有人。于是他请帮手们做了一本巨大的手写书，里面装满了各种棋盘游戏。在厚厚的书页里，画师们画下了欧洲最早记录下来的国际象棋谜题。书里甚至还讲了每一个雕刻的棋子该怎样在棋盘上滑行，又该涂上哪些鲜亮的颜色呢。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: A King's Book of Games in Times of War

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, King Alfonso lived through a loud and scary war, even fighting with his own family. To find a quiet space of peace, he asked his artists to paint a wonderful book filled with the secrets of chess, backgammon, and dice. Inside its colorful pages, he even drew giant chessboards and games that followed the movement of the silent stars.
variants.luca: While battles raged outside his castle walls, King Alfonso decided to launch a totally different kind of mission. In 1283, he finished a master plan of a book packed with rules for chess and dice battles. He even upgraded the adventure by adding giant-sized chess and games played with the actual stars!
variants.cn: 很久很久以前，在西班牙，阿方索国王经历了一场又吵又吓人的战争，连自己的家人都跟他打了起来。为了找到一块安静的小天地，他请画师们画了一本特别棒的书，里面藏着国际象棋、双陆棋和骰子游戏的秘密。在五彩缤纷的书页里，他还画下了巨大的棋盘，以及跟着夜空中静悄悄的星星移动的游戏呢。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a sad king named Alfonso faced a rebellion led by his own son. During a quiet moment of peace, he decided to paint and write a magnificent book all about indoor games. He hoped that the magic of chess would bring a little warmth and comfort to those who were feeling lonely or unwell in their homes.
variants.luca: Imagine your own family turning against you in a battle for the throne! That is exactly what happened to King Alfonso, but he did not give up. In a quick break from the fighting, he launched a brilliant plan to create a master guidebook of games. He wanted chess to be a secret weapon of joy for anyone trapped inside or fighting a tough illness.
variants.cn: 很久以前的西班牙，有一位伤心的国王，名叫阿方索。他的儿子竟然带头反对他。趁着一段难得安静的日子，他决定写一本华丽的大书，画上各种各样能在屋里玩的游戏。他希望国际象棋的魔力，能给那些待在家里、感到孤单或者生病的人，带去一点点温暖和安慰。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: King Alfonso of Spain loved to write down neat, tidy rules to keep his whole land peaceful. He decided his very oldest son would be the next king, drawing it out like a beautiful plan on paper. But when his son passed away, the king learned that even the most carefully written rules cannot control the future.
variants.luca: Alfonso thought he could map out his kingdom's future like a perfect game! He set a super strict law that his firstborn son would take the crown next. But a sudden tragedy crashed through his strategy, proving that real life doesn't always follow the rulebook.
variants.cn: 西班牙的阿方索国王最喜欢把规矩写得整整齐齐，好让整个国家平平安安。他定下规矩：自己最大的儿子将来接着当国王，还像画一幅漂亮的图纸一样，把计划写在纸上。可是后来，他的大儿子不幸去世了。国王这才明白：哪怕规矩写得再仔细，也管不住明天会发生什么。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: A King's Cure for Boredom and Brawls
stories.titleCn: 国王治无聊和吵架的妙方

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a gentle king named Alfonso watched his people argue over noisy dice games. He wanted to give them something quiet and beautiful to soothe their minds instead. So, he helped write a special book about the quiet magic of chess, showing how the pieces could bring comfort to anyone who was feeling sad.
variants.luca: King Alfonso looked out at his kingdom in the 1270s and saw way too many wild brawls over silly bets. He needed a master plan to stop the chaos, so he created a legendary rulebook for a brand new battle of wits. He proved that you could have an epic adventure right on a wooden board without ever throwing a single punch.
variants.cn: 很久以前的西班牙，有一位温和的国王叫阿方索。他看到人们玩吵闹的骰子游戏时总是争吵，心里很着急。他想送给大家一样安静又美好的东西，让人们的心平静下来。于是，他帮忙写了一本特别的书，讲国际象棋那种安安静静的魔力——小小的棋子，也能安慰每一个不开心的人。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a thoughtful king named Alfonso spent his quiet hours writing one of the very first books about chess. He loved how the carved pieces moved safely across the board, but outside his library, a real storm was brewing. His own son, Sancho, wanted to take the golden crown, forcing the father to defend his kingdom with gentle patience.
variants.luca: This wasn't just a quiet game on a board—it was a high-stakes battle for the throne! Prince Sancho launched a rebellion to snatch the crown, forcing King Alfonso to dodge sneaky traps and make secret deals. To survive, the king had to think five moves ahead, just like a real chess master protecting his army.
variants.cn: 很久以前的西班牙，有一位爱思考的国王，名叫阿方索。安静的时候，他就坐下来写书，那可是世界上最早的国际象棋书之一。他喜欢看雕刻的棋子在棋盘上稳稳当当地走来走去。可是在书房外面，一场真正的风暴正在酝酿——他自己的儿子桑乔，想抢走那顶金灿灿的王冠。这位父亲只好用温和又耐心的办法，守护自己的王国。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in India, wise teachers wondered if it was better to be clever or just lucky. They used two games to find the answer. Rolling dice represented the wild winds of chance, but moving chess pieces showed the quiet power of a thoughtful mind.
variants.luca: It was a massive debate! The thinkers of ancient India wanted to know if brainpower could beat random luck. So they set up a battle between rolling dice, which is totally wild, and chess, where you need a brilliant strategy to win.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在印度，有几位充满智慧的老师在琢磨一个问题：到底是聪明更厉害，还是运气更厉害呢？他们用两种游戏来寻找答案。掷骰子就像一阵抓不住的狂风，全凭运气；而走国际象棋的棋子，却显出了爱思考的头脑里那股安静的力量。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: Chess, Dice, and Backgammon
stories.titleCn: 国际象棋、骰子和双陆棋

variants.lucy: Long ago, a thoughtful king wanted to know what helped people succeed the most: deep thinking, simple luck, or a bit of both. His quiet advisors went away to find the perfect answers. They returned with three beautiful games, including a quiet board of carved wooden chess pieces that needed only a clever mind to win.
variants.luca: Imagine the challenge! One inventor brought rolling dice to show how wild luck can rule the world. Another brought backgammon, where you need a great plan but still have to watch the roll of the dice. But the last inventor showed off chess, where there are no lucky bounces and only your bravest moves can save the day.
variants.cn: 很久以前，有一位爱思考的国王想弄明白：人要做成一件事，最靠得住的到底是什么？是动脑筋，是好运气，还是两样都来一点？他那些安静的谋士们各自出发，去寻找最好的答案。回来的时候，他们带来了三种漂亮的游戏，其中就有一副安安静静的木雕国际象棋——要赢下它，只需要一个聪明的脑袋。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: Chess in the Midst of Rebellion

variants.lucy: Long ago in the 1280s, a king named Alfonso was very sick and could not leave his castle in Seville. While there was trouble outside, he sat quietly and gathered all the chess secrets he knew. He turned them into a beautiful book of games to keep his mind peaceful.
variants.luca: Talk about a family showdown! King Alfonso's own son led a rebellion against him, trapping the poor king inside his own palace. But instead of giving up, the king spent his time writing down the ultimate chess strategies. It became one of the very first and most famous game books in Europe.
variants.cn: 很久以前，大约在一二八零年代，有一位叫阿方索的国王病得很重，只能待在塞维利亚的城堡里，哪儿也去不了。外面闹哄哄的，麻烦不断，他却安安静静地坐着，把自己知道的国际象棋秘密一条一条收集起来，写成了一本漂亮的游戏书，让自己的心保持平静。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, four friends would gather around a single board to play a very special game together. Each person guided their own colorful army representing a time of the year, like the fresh green of spring or the quiet white of winter. They even matched their moves to the quiet power of earth, air, water, and fire.
variants.luca: Imagine a massive four-way clash where the seasons themselves went to war on a single board! You could launch a daring attack with the fiery red summer troops, or defend your territory with the dark autumn army. It was a thrilling struggle of nature, pitting wind and waves against solid ground and burning flames.
variants.cn: 很久以前的西班牙，四个朋友会围着同一张棋盘，一起玩一种特别的游戏。每个人指挥一支彩色的小军队，代表一年里的一个季节——有春天那种嫩嫩的绿色，也有冬天那种安静的白色。他们走的每一步棋，还和土、风、水、火这四种安静的大自然力量一一对应呢。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Hundreds of years ago in Spain, a clever king wrote down a beautiful game in his giant book. The board represented the quiet night sky, with delicate pieces carved to look like the moon and glowing planets. Instead of regular chess, players guided these heavenly shapes on a journey through the stars.
variants.luca: Imagine tossing dice to launch Mars and Venus into a cosmic battle! A Spanish king designed this high-energy game to bring the solar system right onto his table. You got to command seven legendary celestial bodies and blast your way across the board.
variants.cn: 几百年前的西班牙，有一位聪明的国王在他的大书里记下了一种美丽的游戏。棋盘代表着安静的夜空，精巧的棋子被雕成月亮和闪闪发光的行星的模样。这可不是普通的国际象棋——玩的人要带着这些天上的小家伙，在星星之间走一场奇妙的旅行。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: Chess vs. Dice: A King's Choice
stories.titleCn: 国际象棋还是骰子？国王的选择

variants.lucy: Long ago, a thoughtful king named Alfonso watched his court play different games. He disliked dice because they relied only on luck, which often made people cheat and argue. Instead, he favored chess, where players sat quietly and used their minds. He believed this gentle game brought out the very best in people.
variants.luca: King Alfonso wanted a real battle of minds, not just lucky rolls. He thought dice games were too wild, leading to sneaky tricks and bad tempers. For him, the ultimate adventure was on the chessboard. That was where a player needed a clever strategy and sharp thinking to win.
variants.cn: 很久以前，有一位爱思考的国王叫阿方索，他常常看宫廷里的人玩各种游戏。他不喜欢骰子，因为骰子全靠运气，还总让人耍赖、吵架。他更喜欢国际象棋——下棋的人安安静静地坐着，用脑子来较量。他相信，这种温和的游戏能让人拿出自己最好的一面。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Many years ago, families had to keep their game boards hidden away because playing for prizes was forbidden in ordinary homes. Only special gaming halls were allowed to host these matches. But on the cozy nights of Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, the rules softened so everyone could share the joy of playing by the fire.
variants.luca: Back in the old days, playing board games for stakes was totally banned unless you went to a designated gaming hall. But on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, the law declared a massive truce. Families could finally challenge each other at home and share the excitement of the game.
variants.cn: 很多年以前，普通人家是不许玩带彩头的游戏的，所以家家户户只好把棋盘藏起来。只有专门的游戏厅，才可以举办这样的比赛。可是一到平安夜和圣诞节那两个暖融融的夜晚，规矩就变温柔了——大家终于可以围着炉火，一起分享玩游戏的快乐啦。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Hundreds of years ago, families gathered around a wooden board to play a quiet game of chase. One person guided a single, swift hare, while their opponent moved twelve tiny pieces to try and circle the little animal. If the clever hare could slip past and take three of those pieces away, it won its freedom. With only nine pursuers left on the board, there was simply too much open space for the hare to ever be caught.
variants.luca: Imagine being one lone player facing an army of twelve hunters closing in from every side! This medieval game was a thrilling race where you had to dodge, weave, and strike back. Your goal as the speedy beast was to knock out enough attackers until only nine remained. Once the enemy force shrunk to nine, their trap crumbled, and you leaped away to victory!
variants.cn: 几百年前，一家人会围着一块木头棋盘，玩一种安安静静的追逐游戏。一个人指挥一只跑得飞快的野兔，对手则移动十二个小小的棋子，想把这只小动物团团围住。如果机灵的野兔能溜过去，吃掉其中三个棋子，它就赢回了自由——因为棋盘上只剩九个追兵的时候，空地实在太多，野兔就再也不会被抓住啦。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: A long time ago, strict laws stopped people from wagering shiny silver coins on their board games. Even risking a loaf of bread or a sweet drink was forbidden, with one very gentle exception. If the two players promised to sit down and share the tasty prize together as soon as the match ended, the law allowed it.
variants.luca: Imagine a time when betting your gold coins on a game could get you into major trouble with the law! To keep the adventure going, players had to find a clever loophole. If you wagered a delicious treat, you and your opponent had to sit down and devour the prize together the second the match ended.
variants.cn: 很久以前，严格的法律不许人们拿亮闪闪的银币当棋局的赌注。就连押上一块面包、一杯甜甜的饮料都不行。不过，有一个特别温柔的例外：只要两位棋手说好，比赛一结束就坐下来，把好吃的奖品一起分享掉，法律就答应啦。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: A very long time ago in Spain, King Alfonso wrote a beautiful book about the secrets of the chessboard. He believed the chess king should be treated with the same deep respect as a real-life ruler. That is why nobody ever removes the king from the board or harms him during a match.
variants.luca: Instead, you have to win by pulling off a clever trap! You corner the leader, block all his escape routes, and force him to run for his life. It is the ultimate royal embarrassment when the mightiest piece on the board has to scramble away in defeat.
variants.cn: 很久很久以前，在西班牙，阿方索国王写了一本漂亮的书，讲棋盘上的种种秘密。他认为，棋盘上的王，应该像现实中的国王一样受到深深的尊重。所以呀，下棋的时候，谁也不会把王从棋盘上拿走，更不会伤害他。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a gentle king named Alfonso wanted to save the games he loved. He gathered artists to paint a giant, beautiful book filled with colorful drawings of chess boards. Because of his quiet care, we can look back through time and see exactly how families played together so many years ago.
variants.luca: Imagine a king from the twelve-hundreds who spent his time collecting the ultimate secrets of chess! King Alfonso packed a mega-book with tricky puzzles and wild game setups. It is like a real-life treasure map that shows us exactly how knights battled on the board!
variants.cn: 很久以前的西班牙，有一位温和的国王叫阿方索，他想把自己心爱的游戏好好保存下来。他召集画师们，画了一本又大又漂亮的书，里面满是色彩鲜艳的国际象棋棋盘图。正因为他这份细心的爱护，今天的我们才能穿过时光，看见那么多年前的一家人是怎样围坐在一起玩游戏的。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: King Alfonso's Medieval Puzzle Book
stories.titleCn: 阿方索国王的中世纪谜题书

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a king named Alfonso loved the quiet beauty of chess. He ordered a giant book to be created, filled with dozens of unique brain-teasers. Each page showed a different challenge, some with only a few pieces left on the board for players to study.
variants.luca: Imagine opening a massive, ancient book of secret tactical battles! King Alfonso created these wild challenges to test the cleverest minds of his time. People back then would spend hours plotting their moves to conquer each difficult board layout. It was the ultimate quest to see who could find the winning path!
variants.cn: 很久以前的西班牙，有一位叫阿方索的国王，深深迷上了国际象棋那种安静的美。他下令做一本巨大的书，里面装满了几十道独一无二的动脑谜题。每一页都是一个不同的挑战，有的棋盘上只剩下几个棋子，等着棋手们细细研究。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: King Alfonso's Rules for Fair Play
stories.titleCn: 阿方索国王的公平游戏规则

variants.lucy: Long ago, the rooms where people gathered to play games were very loud and full of trickery. King Alfonso wanted everyone to enjoy their games in peace, so he decided to make a change. In the year 1276, he had a beautiful book written down with forty-four special rules. This guide helped protect players so that every move on the board could be honest and kind.
variants.luca: Imagine a crowded hall where players used secret tricks and even fake dice to steal a victory. King Alfonso of Castile decided to put an end to this wild chaos. In 1276, he created a powerful law book packed with forty-four rules to stop the cheaters. This brave plan made sure that every game of skill was played with honor.
variants.cn: 很久以前，人们聚在一起玩游戏的屋子总是闹哄哄的，到处都有人耍小花招。阿方索国王希望每个人都能安安心心地玩游戏，于是决定改变这一切。在1276年，他让人写下了一本漂亮的书，里面有四十四条特别的规则。这本指南保护着每一位玩游戏的人，让棋盘上的每一步都诚实又友善。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: King Alfonso's Rules for Wild Gamers
stories.titleCn: 阿方索国王的游戏法典

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, the rooms where people played board games were so noisy and full of arguments that even the judges were baffled. To help everyone, King Alfonso sat down and carefully wrote forty-four laws to bring peace to the tables. He wanted to protect players and make sure every single wager was fair and honest. However, if someone chose to cheat three separate times, they faced a very quiet and permanent punishment.
variants.luca: Picture a medieval hall packed with shouting players, clashing boards, and total chaos! King Alfonso decided to tame this wild scene by launching forty-four brand-new laws for gamers. He drew up strict boundaries for betting to keep the play honest and intense. And if you dared to cheat three times, the penalty was absolutely brutal—you would lose your thumbs!
variants.cn: 很久很久以前，在西班牙，人们下棋玩游戏的屋子里总是吵吵嚷嚷、争个不停，连法官都被弄得晕头转向。为了帮大家解决麻烦，阿方索国王坐下来，认认真真写了四十四条法律，要让每张游戏桌都安安静静、规规矩矩。他想保护每一位玩家，让每一次打赌都公平诚实。不过呀，要是有人忍不住作弊，而且一连作弊三次，就要受到一种悄悄的、再也改不回来的惩罚哦。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: King Alfonso's Speed-Up Dice
stories.titleCn: 阿方索国王的加速骰子

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a gentle king named Alfonso loved playing a massive board game with giant wooden pieces. He watched over games filled with tall giraffes, proud lions, and even magical unicorns. Because the board was so big, the matches lasted for days. To make things faster, the king had his artists carve special blocks with eight sides to choose the next animal's turn.
variants.luca: Imagine a chess battle where you command roaring lions and charging unicorns across a giant board! King Alfonso loved this super-sized game, but the clashes took forever to finish. To speed through the adventure, the king came up with a brilliant plan. He created unique dice with eight sides, forcing players to roll and instantly launch their next beast into the action!
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，有一位温和的国王叫阿方索，他特别喜欢玩一种巨大的棋盘游戏，棋子都是大块的木头雕的。棋盘上有高高的长颈鹿、神气的狮子，甚至还有神奇的独角兽。可是棋盘实在太大啦，一盘棋常常要下上好几天。为了让游戏快一点，国王请工匠们做了一种特别的八面骰子，掷一掷，就知道下一步轮到哪只动物出场了。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: Medieval Soldiers on the Chessboard
stories.titleCn: 棋盘上的中世纪小士兵

variants.lucy: Long ago, a wise king named Alfonso wrote a beautiful book about the secrets of chess. He believed the little pawns were like the quiet foot soldiers of his kingdom, carrying heavy gear on their backs. Because their packs were so heavy, they could only take one small step at a time.
variants.luca: But don't underestimate these soldiers when the battle begins! Alfonso explained that a warrior couldn't easily strike an enemy blocking them face-to-face. Instead, they had to wait for the perfect moment to swing their swords sideways at an opponent on the diagonal.
variants.cn: 很久以前，有一位聪明的国王叫阿方索，他写了一本漂亮的书，专门讲国际象棋里藏着的秘密。他觉得，棋盘上那些小小的兵，就像王国里默默无闻的步兵，背上扛着沉甸甸的装备。正因为背包太重啦，他们每次只能慢慢地、稳稳地向前迈一小步。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Imagine a quiet evening over seven hundred years ago, playing a game where the board is the night sky. Instead of wooden pawns, you guide seven shining planets through the twelve signs of the zodiac. To win, you must carefully watch how these stars align to see if they are friendly or fighting.
variants.luca: This was the ultimate brain championship for the kingdom's cleverest scholars back in 1283! You got to launch seven cosmic planets across a map of the zodiac. To score a victory, you had to calculate exactly how these space pieces clashed or teamed up based on where they landed.
variants.cn: 想象一下，在七百多年前一个安静的夜晚，你玩的棋盘竟然是整片星空！你移动的不是木头小兵，而是七颗闪闪发光的行星，让它们在十二个星座之间慢慢旅行。想要赢，就得仔细观察这些星星排成的样子——看看它们是好朋友，还是正在闹别扭呢。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, King Alfonso noticed that chess matches could last for a very long time. The players would sit quietly, waiting and waiting for the next turn. To bring a soft touch of surprise to the board, they began rolling dice to decide which piece to move next.
variants.luca: Imagine waiting forever just for one single turn. King Alfonso's players solved this boredom by tossing dice right onto the table to make things move much faster. Suddenly, the quiet strategy game became a wild race where a lucky roll decided your next big move.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，阿方索国王发现，一盘国际象棋有时候要下好久好久。棋手们安安静静地坐着，等啊等啊，就为了等对方走下一步。为了给棋盘添上一点小小的惊喜，人们开始掷骰子，让骰子来决定下一步该走哪个棋子。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a wise king named Alfonso created a beautiful, hand-painted book filled with chess secrets. He loved the quiet order of the game, where every piece had its place. Sadly, his own home became much more troubled than any chessboard when his son turned against him to take the crown.
variants.luca: Talk about a massive plot twist! Alfonso's son, Sancho, secretly teamed up with enemy rulers to snatch the kingdom away. The wise king had to spend his very last years defending his throne in a giant, real-life battle. It was just like a high-stakes chess match, but with real crowns on the line.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，有一位聪明的国王叫阿方索，他做了一本美丽的手绘书，里面装满了国际象棋的秘密。他喜欢棋盘上那种安安静静的秩序——每个棋子都待在自己该待的地方。可惜呀，他自己的家却比任何一盘棋都要乱：他的亲生儿子竟然背叛了他，想夺走他的王冠。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: The Cosmic Chess Game of the Stars

variants.lucy: Long ago in the Middle Ages, people played a beautiful game modeled after the evening sky. Instead of ordinary chess pieces, they moved tiny planets, including a sorrowful Saturn draped in a dark, cozy shawl. They watched the real stars above to see how to guide their cosmic pieces.
variants.luca: To launch their celestial armies, players had to roll a strange die with seven different sides. Every single roll sent a planet charging across the board depending on the patterns in the sky. Imagine controlling the entire cosmos with one lucky toss!
variants.cn: 很久以前的中世纪，人们玩一种照着夜空的样子做出来的美丽棋戏。棋盘上摆的不是普通的棋子，而是一颗颗小小的行星，其中还有一颗忧伤的土星，裹着一条深色的、暖暖的披肩。下棋的人会抬头看真正的星星，看看天上的星星怎么排，再决定棋盘上的星星该怎么走。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago, clever teachers created a special board painted with the four times of the year. The squares were divided into bright sections for spring, summer, autumn, and winter. To win, you had to watch the quiet changes of the seasons and guide your pieces carefully through them.
variants.luca: Imagine a medieval clash where the battlefield actually changes with the calendar! Thinkers created a board with colorful zones for spring, summer, autumn, and winter. You had to command your pieces to match the shifting times of the year to win.
variants.cn: 很久以前，一些聪明的学者发明了一种特别的棋盘，上面画着一年里的四个季节。棋盘被分成四块亮闪闪的区域，分别代表春天、夏天、秋天和冬天。想要赢，你就得留心季节悄悄的变化，小心地带着你的棋子，一步一步走过整整一年。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Nearly eight hundred years ago, players loved a highly disciplined version of chess where every single move had to follow strict guidelines. Old stories whisper that clever young women from a faraway shore first created these rules. Because of this sweet tale, people lovingly called the match the game of maidens.
variants.luca: Imagine a fierce chess showdown where the rules are so tight you are forced into your moves. Stories claim this daring challenge was dreamed up by young women living far across the ocean. Everyone called it the game of maidens, and it was the ultimate test of strategy.
variants.cn: 差不多八百年前，棋手们特别喜欢一种规矩特别严的国际象棋，每走一步棋，都必须按照严格的规则来。古老的故事里悄悄传说，最早想出这些规则的，是住在大海对岸的聪明姑娘们。因为这个甜甜的传说，大家都亲切地把这种下法叫作“少女棋”。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: The Giant Chess of Mythical Beasts

variants.lucy: Imagine opening a dusty, hand-painted book from hundreds of years ago to find a board with over one hundred squares. Instead of normal wooden pieces, you would guide gentle unicorns and proud lions across the grid. The most wondrous of all was a giant bird that could lift a whole elephant into the clouds. It was a game meant to show a ruler's quiet majesty.
variants.luca: This wasn't just a regular game; it was an absolute beast of a battle with twenty-four fighters on each side! You got to launch wild attacks using roaring lions and a massive bird called the Aanca. Picture swooping down from the sky to snatch up an entire elephant in your claws. Kings played this giant game to prove they were the toughest rulers around and terrify anyone who dared challenge them.
variants.cn: 想象一下，你翻开一本几百年前落满灰尘的手绘古书，里面画着一张超过一百个格子的大棋盘。在那上面，你指挥的不是普通的木头棋子，而是温柔的独角兽和神气的狮子。最神奇的是一只巨大的鸟，它能叼起一整头大象，飞到云朵上面去！这是一种让国王显得格外威严的游戏。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: The Giant Chess of Wild Beasts

variants.lucy: A long time ago in India, people created a giant chess board that looked like a magical forest. Instead of only standard soldiers, they carved rare, colorful birds and wild creatures to move through the game. Rulers used these beautiful animal figures to show off their great riches to anyone who visited.
variants.luca: Imagine marching a roaring wild predator right across a giant board to terrify your opponent! Ancient rulers used these massive animal pieces to scare their rivals and prove who was boss. It was a wild battle of wits where you could command a whole army of beasts.
variants.cn: 很久很久以前，在印度，人们做出了一张巨大的棋盘，看上去就像一座神奇的森林。棋盘上不只有普通的小士兵，工匠们还雕出了罕见的彩色大鸟和各种野兽，让它们在棋盘上走来走去。国王们就用这些漂亮的动物棋子，向每一位来访的客人炫耀自己的财富。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in sunny Spain, players would sometimes get very upset when their games did not go well. The law back then made you pay a fine if you broke the wooden board with a stone or a blade. But if you were silly enough to crack the board using nothing but your own forehead, you did not have to pay a single coin.
variants.luca: Picture a player getting so wild after losing that they just want to smash the whole game to pieces! Back then, using a rock or a dagger to break the board meant you had to pay a heavy fine. But if you chose to dive headfirst and shatter the wood with your own skull, the law let you off completely free. That is one painful way to save your coins!
variants.cn: 很久以前，在阳光灿烂的西班牙，棋手们输了棋有时会气得不得了。那时候的法律规定：要是你用石头或刀子把木头棋盘砸坏了，就得交罚款。可是，如果你傻乎乎地只用自己的额头把棋盘撞裂了，那就一个铜板都不用交！

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago, a gentle guardian called the Alferza stood right beside the king to keep him safe. This was before the modern queen ever joined the board. On its very first turn, this loyal helper could make a magical hop right over the other pieces to find its perfect spot.
variants.luca: Imagine a medieval bodyguard springing right into battle to defend the king! This lieutenant piece had an incredible secret ability to start the game. It could launch itself into the air, vaulting over other figures to charge straight toward danger.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在现在的“后”还没出现的年代，棋盘上有一位温柔的守护者，叫“阿尔费扎”，它总是紧紧守在王的身边，保护王的安全。在它走的第一步棋里，这位忠心的小帮手还有一个神奇的本领——可以一下子跳过别的棋子，蹦到最合适的位置上去。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a wise king named Alfonso loved to watch his court play chess on different boards. He saw some people try to play on giant wooden grids with over one hundred squares, but the pieces got lost on those endless journeys. In the end, he helped everyone see that the quiet magic of the game fits best on our familiar grid of sixty-four squares.
variants.luca: King Alfonso wanted the ultimate chess battle, but people kept messing up the battlefield size! Some players built giant boards that made games drag on forever like a never-ending march. Others shrunk the board so tiny that the clash was over in a blink. Finally, they locked in the classic eight-by-eight grid for the perfect showdown.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，聪明的阿方索国王喜欢看大臣们用各种各样的棋盘下棋。他见过有人在一百多个格子的大棋盘上玩，可棋子们在那么大的地方走啊走啊，就像迷了路一样。最后，国王帮大家明白了一个道理：国际象棋安安静静的魔力，最适合我们熟悉的那张六十四格棋盘。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, the bishop on the chessboard was carved to look like a quiet, powerful elephant. A wise king named Alfonso wrote that a ruler should never travel to war with just one of these gentle giants. If one became too tired or hurt, there would always be a second companion ready to help protect the kingdom.
variants.luca: King Alfonso had a brilliant battle plan: never charge into a fight with only one giant war elephant! He insisted on bringing a pair of these massive beasts to charge across the board. That way, if your first heavy hitter got knocked out, the backup elephant could stampede right in to save the day.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，棋盘上的“象”真的被雕成了大象的样子——安静又有力气的大块头。聪明的阿方索国王在书里写道：国王出门打仗，千万不能只带一头大象。万一这头大象累了、受伤了，旁边还有第二个伙伴，随时准备顶上来，保护整个王国。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a wise king named Alfonso collected over one hundred chess challenges into a beautiful, hand-written book. He wanted to share these quiet mind-games with everyone, but a few of the drawings had tiny mistakes that made them impossible to finish. For hundreds of years, these little errors slept on the pages until modern chess lovers finally solved the mystery.
variants.luca: Imagine opening a book of chess battles from many centuries ago, only to find out the games are completely stuck. King Alfonso designed over a hundred of these challenges, but a few had hidden mistakes that made winning totally impossible. It took modern chess detectives to hunt down the errors and finally crack the king's broken codes.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，聪明的阿方索国王把一百多道国际象棋难题，收进了一本美丽的手写书里。他想把这些安安静静的动脑游戏分享给所有人。可是有几幅图画上出了一点点小差错，让那些题目根本没办法解开。这些小错误在书页里一睡就是好几百年，直到现代的棋迷们当起了侦探，才终于解开了谜团。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago, a king ordered a wonderful book filled with over a hundred chess secrets. Artists painted colorful illustrations for every single page to show where the wooden pieces belonged. If you look closely at the drawings, you can see exactly how to set up each challenge.
variants.luca: This wasn't just a regular book—it was a battle guide with high-stakes challenges. You had to hunt down the perfect checkmate in a limited number of turns. One tiny slip-up by the attacker, and the defender snatched the victory instantly.
variants.cn: 很久以前，一位国王下令做一本很棒的书，里面藏着一百多个国际象棋的秘密。画师们给每一页都画上了五彩缤纷的插图，告诉你每个木头棋子应该摆在哪里。只要你仔细看那些图画，就能照着摆出每一道棋题来。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a wise king named Alfonso put together a beautiful book filled with chess secrets. Inside, there was a riddle about a lone white knight surrounded by danger. To save himself, the horse had to leap sixteen times, tapping the enemy king with every single jump.
variants.luca: This was the ultimate high-stakes escape mission. If that knight paused for even a single turn, a heavy enemy rook was ready to slide in and end the game. The brave little horse had to launch sixteen perfect attacks in a row without making a single mistake.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，聪明的阿方索国王编了一本美丽的书，里面装满了国际象棋的秘密。书里有一道谜题，讲的是一匹孤零零的白马，被危险团团围住。想要救自己，这匹马必须连着跳十六次，而且每跳一下，都要刚好将对方的王一军！

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Once in ancient India, a king asked his advisors to show him whether clever planning or simple luck guides our lives. One advisor brought rolling dice, another brought a game of mixed chance, but the last one quietly presented a beautiful chessboard. The ruler gazed at the carved pieces and decided that this thoughtful game of pure skill was the most wonderful of all.
variants.luca: Imagine a royal challenge where three thinkers had to prove what rules the world: brainpower, wild luck, or a bit of each! One competitor brought dice for chaotic chance, and another brought a game where skill fights back against bad luck. But the winner brought a chessboard to prove that a sharp mind wins every single battle. The king absolutely loved chess, declaring it the greatest and most respectable game of all!
variants.cn: 从前，在古老的印度，有一位国王问他的三位谋士：到底是聪明的计划，还是单纯的运气，在指引我们的生活？一位谋士带来了骰子，另一位带来了一种又靠运气又靠本事的游戏，最后一位却安安静静地捧出一张漂亮的国际象棋棋盘。国王看着那些精雕细刻的棋子，最后决定：这种全靠动脑的游戏，才是世界上最美妙的游戏。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago in medieval Spain, a wise king named Alfonso loved to study beautiful chess puzzles. One of these ancient mind-teasers was packed with twenty-nine wooden pieces, filling almost every square on the board. It looked like a quiet, crowded forest waiting for a spark of magic.
variants.luca: To solve this ultimate challenge, the black side had to launch a daring, non-stop attack. A single, brave rook had to charge across the board and put the enemy king in danger twelve times in a row without stopping. One wrong move would ruin the whole mission, but a perfect run meant total victory.
variants.cn: 很久很久以前，在中世纪的西班牙，有一位聪明的国王，名叫阿方索。他最喜欢研究漂亮的国际象棋谜题啦。其中有一道古老的谜题，棋盘上密密麻麻摆了二十九个木头棋子，几乎把每个格子都占满了。看上去就像一片安安静静、挤挤挨挨的小森林，正等着一点魔法的火花呢。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Eight hundred years ago, a gentle king in Spain named Alfonso wanted everyone to share his love for chess. He asked artists to paint a grand book filled with bright scenes of friends sitting together over the game boards. This precious book even had rules written down so that every player in the land would be treated with kindness and respect.
variants.luca: Imagine a medieval king who was so obsessed with board games that he made them the law of the land! King Alfonso ordered his scribes to create a massive, action-packed handbook showing players matching wits. He even set up strict kingdom-wide rules to stop any sneaky cheaters in their tracks.
variants.cn: 八百年前，西班牙有一位温和的国王，名叫阿方索。他特别希望大家都能像他一样爱上国际象棋。于是他请画师们画了一本华丽的大书，里面满是朋友们围坐在棋盘边下棋的鲜亮画面。这本宝贝书里还写下了规则，好让全国每一位下棋的人都能受到善待和尊重。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: The King Who Loved Indoor Games

variants.lucy: High up in his castle eight hundred years ago, a gentle Spanish king named Alfonso sat down to write a massive, beautiful book all about board games. He knew that when life felt dark or cold, a simple chess board could bring a quiet spark of happiness. He loved how the little wooden pieces could be played anywhere, even by someone keeping dry indoors while the rain tapped on the window pane.
variants.luca: Imagine playing chess while your ship tosses and turns on giant, stormy waves! King Alfonso thought that was the ultimate adventure, so he put it all in his giant gaming rulebook. He wanted everyone to have a blast with chess, whether they were locked up in a secret tower or just hiding from a massive storm. All you needed was a board and a clever plan to start your own tabletop quest.
variants.cn: 八百年前，在高高的城堡里，温和的西班牙国王阿方索坐下来，开始写一本又大又漂亮的书，专门讲各种棋类游戏。他知道，当日子又冷又灰暗的时候，一张小小的棋盘也能点亮一束安静的快乐。他最喜欢这些小木棋子走到哪儿都能玩——哪怕外面下着雨，雨点敲着窗户，你躲在屋里也照样可以下上一盘。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: The King Who Wanted to Cure Sadness

variants.lucy: Hundreds of years ago, a gentle king named Alfonso noticed that his people were carrying heavy worries. To help them feel better, he created a massive, beautiful book filled with colorful hand-painted drawings of chess boards. He believed that moving these tiny wooden pieces could help a tired mind find peace and quiet joy.
variants.luca: King Alfonso launched a grand plan to defeat sadness using the power of board games! He packed a giant book with the most exciting chess puzzles he could find. It was his secret weapon to get everyone's brain working and turn their gloomy days into a playful adventure.
variants.cn: 几百年前，温和的国王阿方索发现，他的子民们心里装着沉甸甸的烦恼。为了让大家开心起来，他做了一本又大又美的书，里面满是手绘的彩色棋盘图画。他相信，挪动这些小小的木头棋子，能让疲惫的脑袋安静下来，找到平和又暖暖的快乐。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago, a wise king named Alfonso wrote a beautiful book about the secrets of chess. He loved how the clever knight could hop gracefully across the board. He showed how one lone horseman, starting in the very corner, could touch every square on the board during its quiet journey.
variants.luca: Imagine a wild mission where your knight has to leap onto every single square on the battlefield without missing one! King Alfonso wrote down this ultimate jumping quest hundreds of years ago. Today, brave players still try to solve this legendary puzzle called the Knight's Tour.
variants.cn: 很久以前，聪明的国王阿方索写了一本漂亮的书，讲国际象棋的小秘密。他特别喜欢看机灵的马在棋盘上轻巧地跳来跳去。他还展示了一匹孤零零的小马，从棋盘的角落出发，怎样在安静的旅行中踩遍棋盘上的每一个格子。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: The Limited Leap of the Medieval Bishop
stories.titleCn: 中世纪小象的短短一跳

variants.lucy: More than seven hundred years ago, the bishop was a quiet traveler on the wooden board. King Alfonso wrote in his old book that this little piece could only ever visit six special squares. It moved by taking a gentle, two-step leap along the diagonal lines, never wandering any further.
variants.luca: Back in the medieval days, the bishop didn't slide across the whole battlefield like a rocket. It was a trick jumper, leaping exactly two spaces diagonally to land on its target. This meant the brave piece was locked out of almost every fight, with only six spots it could ever reach!
variants.cn: 七百多年前，象还是木头棋盘上一位安安静静的小旅行家。国王阿方索在他的古书里写道，这枚小棋子一辈子只能去六个特别的格子。它走路的方式，是沿着斜线轻轻一跳、正好跳过两格，再远的地方就从来不去啦。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: The Medieval Game of Forced Chess

variants.lucy: Long ago in medieval Spain, players loved a quiet puzzle game where the rules were turned upside down. If a wooden piece stepped into your path, you were absolutely required to take it, even if it felt like a trap. It was a gentle lesson in letting go, where giving away your own pieces on purpose was the secret to finding a victory.
variants.luca: Imagine a wild battle from seven centuries ago where you are forced to strike every target your enemy throws at you! In this Spanish game, you couldn't run away or ignore an invitation to fight. You had to charge forward and capture, meaning you could sacrifice your mightiest warriors to lure the enemy into a trap. To win this clash, you actually had to lose your army on purpose!
variants.cn: 很久以前，在中世纪的西班牙，棋手们喜欢玩一种把规则整个翻过来的安静小游戏。只要有棋子走到你跟前，你就必须把它吃掉——哪怕你觉得那是个圈套，也不能不吃。这其实是一堂温柔的“学会放手”课：故意把自己的棋子送出去，反而是赢棋的秘密呢。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: The Real-Life Battles of a Chess King

variants.lucy: Long ago, a king named Alfonso spent his quiet hours creating a magnificent book filled with chess secrets. But while he was traveling far from home, a real army crossed into his peaceful lands. His young son had to step forward and watch over the kingdom.
variants.luca: Picture this: the king is away, and suddenly an enemy army marches right into your territory! In the year 1275, King Alfonso's young son had to face this exact challenge. He had to act fast and protect his family's land all by himself.
variants.cn: 很久以前，国王阿方索常常在安静的时光里，编写一本装满国际象棋秘密的华丽大书。可是有一次，他出门远行，一支真正的军队竟闯进了他平静的国土。他年纪小小的儿子只好勇敢地站出来，替父亲守护整个王国。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: The Sad King and His Book of Games
stories.titleCn: 伤心的国王和他的游戏书

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a gentle king named Alfonso faced deep sadness when his own family started a war against him. To find a quiet space in his mind, he turned to the beautiful, carved shapes of chess pieces. He asked his scribes to paint a magnificent book filled with pictures of people playing games together. It was his way of finding a little bit of peace when the world outside was so loud.
variants.luca: King Alfonso was in giant trouble when his own relatives turned against him and started a massive fight for the throne! Instead of panicking during the chaos, he made a brilliant, unexpected move. He gathered artists to write one of the greatest game books in history, packed with chess secrets. He showed everyone that even when your kingdom is messy, you can still master the board!
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，温和的国王阿方索遇上了一件特别伤心的事——他自己的家人竟然起兵和他打仗。为了让心里安静一点，他把目光投向那些雕刻得漂漂亮亮的棋子。他请书写师们画了一本华丽的大书，里面全是人们一起开心下棋的画面。外面的世界吵吵嚷嚷，这就是他给自己找到的一小片宁静。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: The Sad King's Book of Games

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a very sad king named Alfonso sat in his quiet palace while a war raged outside. His own family had turned against him, which made his heart ache with sorrow. To find comfort, he spent his very last days in Seville creating a gorgeous book filled with painted chess games. He wanted to show the world that even when everything is loud and scary, a wooden board can bring quiet peace.
variants.luca: Imagine facing a massive rebellion led by your very own relatives. That is exactly what happened to King Alfonso, but instead of giving up, he launched a brilliant final mission. In the city of Seville, he rushed to finish the ultimate guide to chess before his time ran out. It was his way of conquering the chaos, proving that a clever mind on a game board is stronger than any army.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，有一位非常伤心的国王，名叫阿方索。宫殿外战火纷飞，他独自坐在安静的宫殿里。他自己的家人都背叛了他，这让他的心疼得不得了。为了找一点安慰，他在塞维利亚度过的最后那些日子里，做出了一本无比精美的书，里面画满了一局又一局的国际象棋。他想告诉全世界：哪怕外面又吵又吓人，一张小小的木头棋盘，也能带来安安静静的平和。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: If we could look at a very old book, we would discover that the quiet bishop on your board used to be a magnificent war elephant. These grand animals walked along the diagonal paths of the kingdom rather than straight ahead. It was a gentle way to travel because no one could stand against their immense power in a direct fight.
variants.luca: Picture a giant war elephant charging right into the action where your bishop now stands! Hundreds of years ago, a writer explained that these beasts were too powerful for anyone to fight face-to-face. That is why they leaped diagonally across the board, launching clever sideways attacks that nobody could block!
variants.cn: 要是我们能翻开一本特别古老的书，就会发现：你棋盘上那枚安安静静的象，从前竟是一头威风凛凛的战象！这些大家伙在王国里走的是斜斜的路线，而不是一直往前冲。这样走其实很温柔——因为真要面对面打起来，谁也扛不住它们那股巨大的力气呀。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: Three Games for a Wise King
stories.titleCn: 献给智慧国王的三种游戏

variants.lucy: A curious king in ancient India spent his days wondering if we win by making clever choices or just by being lucky. To help him, three wise thinkers arrived with different treasures. One offered the quiet, thoughtful game of chess to show the power of a clever mind, while the others brought rolling dice and a game that blended both together. Many years later, a Spanish ruler named Alfonso loved this tale so much that he saved it forever in his own special book.
variants.luca: This king wanted to solve a major mystery: does victory come from pure, brilliant strategy, or just a lucky roll? The first wise guide stepped up and handed him chess, a battlefield of pure mind power with no luck involved at all. Then came the wild roll of the dice, and finally a game that combined both forces. King Alfonso of Spain thought this clash was so cool that he wrote the whole adventure down in his own book!
variants.cn: 古时候，印度有一位好奇的国王，整天琢磨一个问题：人到底是靠聪明的选择取胜，还是光靠运气？为了帮他解开疑惑，三位智者带着不同的宝贝来了。一位献上了安静又费脑筋的国际象棋，证明聪明脑瓜的力量；另外两位，一个带来了骨碌碌滚的骰子，一个带来了把两样都掺在一起的游戏。许多年以后，西班牙的国王阿方索太喜欢这个故事了，就把它写进自己那本特别的书里，永远地保存了下来。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: If you could peek inside a very old book of games, you would see how different the chess board used to look. Standing right beside the swift horses were giant elephants carved from smooth stone. On their wide backs, these great creatures carried tiny wooden castles filled with miniature soldiers.
variants.luca: Imagine sending giant armored elephants charging across the board instead of quiet bishops! These massive stone beasts stood right next to the leaping horses, ready to crash through the enemy lines. They even carried wooden towers on their backs, packed with tiny soldiers waiting to join the fight!
variants.cn: 要是你能偷偷翻开一本很老很老的游戏书，就会看到从前的棋盘和现在多么不一样。在飞快的马儿旁边，站着用光滑石头雕成的大象。这些大家伙宽宽的背上，还驮着小小的木头城堡，城堡里挤满了迷你小士兵呢。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

variants.lucy: Long ago, a wise Spanish ruler named King Alfonso explained why our chess king takes such tiny, quiet steps. He believed that a true leader never runs in a hurry or panics. Instead, the king walks slowly to look closely at each of his brave soldiers and keep them safe.
variants.luca: You might think a king should charge ahead on a fast horse, but an old Spanish ruler named Alfonso had a far better plan. He wrote that a great commander must never sprint into a trap. By moving just one square at a time, the leader can scout the battlefield and guide his whole army to victory.
variants.cn: 很久以前，西班牙聪明的国王阿方索解释过，为什么棋盘上的王每次只迈小小的、安安静静的一步。他觉得，一位真正的首领从不慌慌张张地乱跑。王慢慢地走，是为了把每一个勇敢的士兵都看仔细，护他们周全。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón

stories.title: A Royal Night at the Opera

variants.lucy: Over a hundred years ago, a quiet young man named Paul sat in a cozy theater box in Paris. While the opera singers performed on stage, he focused on a tiny wooden board. He played a friendly game of chess against two noblemen, gently placing his pieces under the dim lights.
variants.luca: Paul launched a brilliant and fearless attack! He gave up his most valuable pieces on purpose to trap the enemy king. That wild evening turned into the most famous casual chess battle of all time.
variants.cn: 一百多年前，在巴黎，一位安静的年轻人——保罗，坐在剧院里舒舒服服的包厢里。台上的歌唱家们唱着歌剧，他的眼睛却盯着一张小小的木头棋盘。在昏黄的灯光下，他轻轻地落子，和两位贵族下了一盘友好的国际象棋。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: Nearly a century ago, a clever player named Alexander guided his two quiet knights to the very middle of the board. His opponent, George, felt much too cramped with those pieces so close, so he decided to sweep one away. But as soon as that wooden horse left its square, a secret path opened up for the rest of Alexander's army to glide forward.
variants.luca: Back in 1925, Alexander pulled off a daring stunt by marching his knights straight into the heart of the battlefield. George felt completely trapped by these invaders, so he eagerly swiped one of them. But that play was a trap, because losing the piece unlocked a secret gateway for the rest of his army to charge ahead!
variants.cn: 差不多一百年前，有位聪明的棋手，名叫亚历山大。他把自己两匹安静的马，一步一步领到了棋盘正中央。对手乔治被这两个棋子挤得难受极了，就决定吃掉一匹。可那匹木头马刚一离开格子，一条秘密通道就打开了，亚历山大剩下的大军顺着它轻轻滑了上来。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: A thoughtful player named Aron wanted everyone to see the board in a gentle, clever way. He carefully wrote down his new rules for a newspaper in Vienna, showing how pieces can find safe homes to rest. To him, these quiet pathways were like hidden jewels that made his strategy shine.
variants.luca: Aron loved to brag about his daring new battle plans! He declared that he had cracked the secret code of the open pathways on the board. He published his bold rules for everyone to see, showing off the treasures of his wild new system.
variants.cn: 有一位爱思考的棋手，名叫阿伦。他想让大家用一种温和又聪明的眼光来看棋盘。他认认真真地把自己的新规则写下来，登在维也纳的报纸上，告诉大家棋子怎样找到安全的小窝休息。在他心里，这些安静的通道就像藏起来的宝石，让他的战术闪闪发光。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: A wise chess teacher from the past named Aron loved to paint pictures with his words. He said that attacking a row of highly protected pawns is like trying to chew on a hard stone. Instead of rushing in, we must guide our pieces on a quiet, patient journey to find a hidden way through.
variants.luca: Imagine charging your army straight into a wall of solid rock! A brilliant player named Aron warned that crashing into those super-defended targets will only break your own forces. The real adventure is in sneaking your pieces around, tricking the enemy until their strong defense finally cracks.
variants.cn: 从前有位很有智慧的国际象棋老师，名叫阿伦。他特别喜欢用话语来画画。他说，去攻打一排被保护得严严实实的兵，就像啃一块硬邦邦的大石头。所以别急着往里冲，我们要带着棋子来一场安静、耐心的小旅行，找到一条藏起来的路穿过去。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: A grandmaster named Aron looked closely at his wooden figures and saw a tiny world of feelings. He believed the shapes on the board could feel happy and supportive. When they stood side-by-side to protect a square, he said they were showing sweet appreciation for each other's help.
variants.luca: Aron treated his chess games like wild, living adventures. Instead of plain game pieces, his army was full of brave teammates who celebrated every victory. When they teamed up to secure a spot, Aron said they were shouting out loud thanks and showing true friendship on the board.
variants.cn: 有一位特级大师，名叫阿伦。他凑近看自己的木头棋子，竟看见了一个小小的感情世界。他相信棋盘上的这些小家伙会开心，也会互相打气。当它们肩并肩守住一个格子时，他说，它们是在甜甜地感谢对方帮了自己的忙呢。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: In the year 1929, a thoughtful player named Aron Nimzowitsch traveled to a major contest in Carlsbad. Almost everyone expected the famous former champion, Capablanca, to easily win. But Aron guided his pieces with highly unusual, clever ideas that puzzled his opponents. In the end, his quiet focus earned him the top prize.
variants.luca: Aron went head-to-head with the biggest giants of the game, including the famous master Capablanca. Instead of playing safe, he unleashed daring and unexpected plans that shook up the whole room. He charged past the favorites to snatch the gold. That day, he proved his wild style could defeat the toughest opponents on Earth!
variants.cn: 1929年，一位爱思考的棋手——阿龙·尼姆佐维奇——来到卡尔斯巴德，参加一场重要的大赛。几乎所有人都觉得，冠军肯定是那位大名鼎鼎的前世界冠军卡帕布兰卡。可是阿龙走的棋又新奇又巧妙，把对手们一个个都看糊涂了。最后，靠着安安静静的专注，他捧走了第一名的奖杯。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

stories.title: Don't Stop to Clean Your Nose!

variants.lucy: A long time ago, a wise chess master named Aron Nimzowitsch compared the start of a game to a fast running race. He said that if you waste your early turns, it is just like pausing to wipe a speck of dust off your nose while sprinting. It is lovely to be tidy, but pausing for even a second lets your opponent slip right past you.
variants.luca: Imagine you are zooming down the track, sprinting for the finish line! If you stop to clean your face mid-dash, your rival will fly right past you to victory. That is why Nimzowitsch warned players never to waste their very first moves on the board. You have to charge ahead with your pieces right from the start!
variants.cn: 很久以前，有一位聪明的国际象棋大师，名叫阿龙·尼姆佐维奇。他说，下棋的开局就像一场飞快的赛跑。如果你把开头的几步棋浪费掉了，就好像在冲刺的时候，停下来擦掉鼻子上的一点小灰尘。爱干净当然好，可是哪怕只停一秒钟，对手就会“嗖”地一下从你身边冲过去啦。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

stories.title: Lasker's Golden Rule for Pawns
stories.titleCn: 拉斯克的小兵黄金法则

variants.lucy: Long ago, a wise world champion named Emanuel Lasker shared a secret for the very start of a chess game. He believed we should gently nudge just one or two of our little pawns forward at first. This opens up cozy pathways so our noble knights and elegant bishops can step onto the board. If we push too many pawns, our other friends get trapped behind them and lose their turn to play.
variants.luca: Imagine your knights and bishops are heroes waiting for the signal to charge forward. If you spend all your time marching a whole army of pawns, your best fighters stay stuck at the back. Lasker's top rule is to launch just one or two pawns to clear the gates, then send your heavy cavalry leaping into action. Speed is everything when you want to win the center of the board!
variants.cn: 很久以前，一位睿智的世界冠军——埃马努埃尔·拉斯克——分享了一个开局的小秘密。他说，刚开始下棋的时候，只要轻轻推动一两个小兵就够了。这样就能打开舒舒服服的小路，让威风的马和优雅的象走上棋盘。要是推出去的兵太多，其他伙伴就会被堵在后面，连出场的机会都没有啦。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: A long time ago, a wise teacher named Aron Nimzowitsch taught people to treat every single wooden piece on the board with the same gentle care. He believed that each pawn, knight, and rook has its own quiet purpose. If you send just one favorite piece out on a long, lonely journey, the rest of your friends are left behind with nothing to do.
variants.luca: Aron Nimzowitsch had an awesome plan for starting a match! He warned players never to send a single hero charging across the board all by themselves. To win the battle, your entire squad has to team up and move together.
variants.cn: 很久以前，有一位智慧的老师，名叫阿龙·尼姆佐维奇。他教大家要用同样温柔的心，对待棋盘上的每一个棋子。他相信，每个兵、每匹马、每辆车，都有自己安安静静的使命。如果你只派最喜欢的那一个棋子，孤零零地跑去远方冒险，剩下的伙伴们就只能留在原地，什么也做不了。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

stories.title: Nimzowitsch's Golden Rule
stories.titleCn: 尼姆佐维奇的黄金法则

variants.lucy: Long ago, a wise chess teacher named Aron Nimzowitsch shared a quiet secret to keeping your pieces safe. He taught that we should never let a single piece go hunting for lonely enemy pawns before the rest of our army has even woken up. If you rush ahead too quickly, your sleepy friends at home won't be ready to help when trouble arrives.
variants.luca: Imagine charging straight into enemy territory just to snatch a tiny pawn while your knights and bishops are still sitting on their starting squares! Aron Nimzowitsch warned that this greedy shortcut leads straight to disaster. You have to get your whole team ready for action first, or the opponent will trap you in a flash!
variants.cn: 很久以前，聪明的棋艺老师阿龙·尼姆佐维奇悄悄告诉大家一个保护棋子的秘诀。他说，在自己的大部队还没“睡醒”之前，千万别让一个棋子独自跑出去，追着对方孤零零的小兵不放。要是你冲得太快，家里那些还在打瞌睡的伙伴们，等麻烦找上门的时候可帮不上忙哦。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

stories.title: The Boy Who Only Wanted Fireworks

variants.lucy: Long ago, a young player named Aron only wanted his chess pieces to dance in wild, fiery patterns. He ignored the quiet, patient moves, focusing only on big storms on the board until those storms turned against him. To heal his game, he spent years quietly designing a beautiful, brand-new way to guide his pieces.
variants.luca: Teenaged Aron wanted total chaos and spectacular explosions on the chessboard! But after getting crushed in battle after battle, he realized his wild charges weren't working. So, he spent years drawing up a secret blueprint for a completely new style of chess warfare.
variants.cn: 很久以前，有个年轻棋手叫阿龙，他只想让自己的棋子跳又疯又烈的“烟花舞”。他瞧不上那些安静、耐心的走法，一心只想在棋盘上掀起大风暴——直到这些风暴反过来打败了他自己。为了治好自己的棋，他花了好多年时间，悄悄设计出一套漂亮的、全新的下棋方法。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

stories.title: The Center Pawn as a Dangerous Criminal
stories.titleCn: 中心兵是个危险的逃犯

variants.lucy: A long time ago, a thoughtful chess master named Aron Nimzowitsch taught his students to look closely at the very middle of the board. He warned that a free pawn marching down the center was like a sneaky troublemaker on the run. To keep your side safe, you had to work together to quietly stop this traveler in its tracks, or gently remove it from the game.
variants.luca: This master, Aron, wanted players to treat that runaway center pawn like an outlaw on the loose! You had to launch a giant mission with your pieces to corner him. Your only choices were to lock him in a deep dungeon so he could never move, or defeat him right on the spot.
variants.cn: 很久以前，爱思考的国际象棋大师阿龙·尼姆佐维奇教学生们，要紧紧盯着棋盘的正中央。他提醒大家：一个沿着中路大步前进、没人拦着的小兵，就像一个正在逃跑的捣蛋鬼。想保住自己的阵地，就得让棋子们齐心协力——要么悄悄把这个“旅行者”拦在半路上，要么干脆请它离开棋盘。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: A new player once found a quiet way to rescue a difficult game. By sliding a piece back and forth, they kept the opposing king trapped in an endless loop. But the player grew restless with this soft rhythm and decided to move a different castle instead. That tiny change broke the spell, letting the king slip away and costing them the game.
variants.luca: This player had a perfect defensive loop going, keeping a tough opponent locked down with repeated attacks. But then they got tired of the same safe march and decided to swap pieces just to show off. Huge mistake! The rival king saw the gap, bolted for freedom, and snatched the victory right away.
variants.cn: 有个刚学棋的新手，曾经找到一个安安静静的办法，把一盘很难下的棋救了回来。他让一个棋子来来回回地走，把对方的王困在一个绕不出去的圈圈里。可是走着走着，他觉得这样的节奏太没意思了，于是决定换另一辆车来走。就是这么一个小小的改变，魔法一下子被打破了——王溜走了，这盘棋也输掉了。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: Long ago, a chess master named Aron Nimzowitsch looked at his wooden pieces and saw a tiny, living world. He believed the rooks on the board were the closest of friends, always watching out for each other. When one rook stepped into danger to let the other win the game, Aron saw it as a quiet, beautiful act of love.
variants.luca: Imagine your castle pieces as ultimate teammates on a daring mission! Aron Nimzowitsch loved to plan these wild rescues where one rook would charge straight into the enemy line. By drawing all the fire, this brave hero cleared the path so their best buddy could swoop in for the final checkmate. It was the ultimate sacrifice play!
variants.cn: 很久以前，国际象棋大师阿龙·尼姆佐维奇看着自己的木头棋子，仿佛看见了一个小小的、活生生的世界。他相信，棋盘上的两辆车是最要好的朋友，总是互相照应。当一辆车勇敢地走进危险，好让另一辆车赢下棋局时，阿龙觉得，那是一份安静又美丽的爱。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

stories.title: The Funny Way to Teach Chess

variants.lucy: A long time ago, a chess master named Aron decided that learning this game should never feel like dusty homework. He wrote books filled with gentle laughter, comparing the quiet wooden pieces to things we see in our everyday lives. By sharing these cozy stories, he helped people see the deep secrets of the board without getting tired.
variants.luca: Other teachers back then wanted everyone to study silent, boring rules, but Aron completely broke the mold with his wild jokes! He turned tough board battles into exciting adventures by using hilarious, everyday comparisons. He showed everyone that the bravest plans actually start with a giant smile.
variants.cn: 很久以前，有位叫阿龙的国际象棋大师，他觉得学下棋不应该像写灰扑扑的作业那样无聊。他写的书里装满了温和的笑声，把安静的木头棋子比作我们生活里常见的东西。靠着这些暖融融的小故事，他让大家轻轻松松就看懂了棋盘上的大秘密，一点儿也不觉得累。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: More than a hundred years ago, a quiet storm brewed between two great chess thinkers. A young writer named Aron began questioning the traditional rules that players had followed for decades. He showed everyone how to guard the heart of the board with gentle, clever setups from a distance.
variants.luca: Aron decided to throw out the old rulebook and challenge the reigning master, Siegbert, to a battle of ideas! Instead of just rushing pawns straight into the middle, he launched a daring strategy that caught everyone by surprise. This bold move completely transformed how we play the game today.
variants.cn: 一百多年前，两位伟大的棋坛思想家之间，悄悄酝酿着一场风暴。一位名叫阿龙的年轻作者，开始质疑大家遵守了几十年的老规矩。他向所有人展示：原来不用一头挤进去，也可以从远处用轻巧聪明的布局，守护棋盘的中心。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: A clever chess master named Aron lived a long time ago, and he believed every wooden piece on the board had its own little heart. He warned that if you attack an opponent's pawn without a good plan, that tiny soldier will actually giggle at your mistake. To quiet its soft laughter, you must find a way to gently but firmly block its path.
variants.luca: That is when you launch a daring rescue mission with your bravest knight! You gallop right up to the giggling pawn's nose and claim a permanent outpost. Suddenly, your opponent gets super nervous, and that noisy little pawn completely loses its voice.
variants.cn: 很久以前，有位聪明的国际象棋大师叫阿龙，他相信棋盘上的每个木头棋子都有一颗小小的心。他提醒大家：要是你还没想好计划就去攻击对方的兵，那个小士兵真的会咯咯地笑话你哦。想让它的笑声安静下来，你就得想个办法，温柔又坚定地挡住它的路。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: Long ago, a chess master named Aron began a game with one of his corner castles completely missing from the board. Instead of worrying, he guided his little foot soldiers slowly and carefully into the very heart of the battlefield. They stood shoulder to shoulder, creating a safe path while the other player overlooked the middle of the board. It took only thirteen quiet steps for the opponent to realize his own king was entirely lost.
variants.luca: Aron started the match with a giant handicap, leaving his left rook completely off the board! But he had a wild plan to charge his pawns straight down the center like a runaway train. The other player grabbed extra pieces but forgot to guard his own middle ground. In just thirteen lightning-fast moves, the enemy king was trapped with absolutely nowhere to run!
variants.cn: 很久以前，国际象棋大师阿龙下了一盘特别的棋——开局的时候，他角落里的一辆车干脆没放上棋盘。他一点儿也不慌，慢慢地、小心地带着他的小兵们走向战场的正中央。小兵们肩并着肩，铺出一条安全的路，而对手却一直没把棋盘中央放在眼里。只走了短短十三步，对手就发现，自己的王已经彻底没救了。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

stories.title: The Rebel Who Changed Chess
stories.titleCn: 改变国际象棋的叛逆者

variants.lucy: A hundred years ago, a thoughtful player named Aron looked at the wooden pieces and decided to find a new path. The traditional masters shook their heads, warning children not to copy his unusual style. But Aron patiently kept playing his own way, quietly winning giant tournaments and changing the game forever.
variants.luca: Aron didn't care about the dusty old rules! While everyone else played it safe, he launched brave, surprising attacks that left his opponents completely scrambled. He swept through the biggest tournaments of his time, proving that a little rebellion can completely rewrite the game.
variants.cn: 一百年前，有位爱思考的棋手叫阿龙，他望着木头棋子，决定走一条新路。那些守旧的大师们直摇头，还告诫孩子们千万别学他那奇怪的下法。可阿龙耐心地坚持自己的风格，悄悄地赢下了一个又一个大比赛，把这项游戏永远地改变了。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

stories.title: The Schoolyard Chess Fight
stories.titleCn: 操场上的国际象棋大战

variants.lucy: A long time ago, a thoughtful chess master named Aron Nimzowitsch used a clever playground story to teach his students. He explained that to win a weak pawn, you do not have to attack it directly. Instead, you gently steer its defenders away or block their path so they can no longer help.
variants.luca: Get ready for a classic schoolyard showdown right on the board! Aron Nimzowitsch loved to show players how to capture a weak pawn by ignoring the pawn itself at first. Your real mission is to charge at the defenders, scaring them off or blocking them completely. Once the guards scatter, that target is totally yours!
variants.cn: 很久以前，爱思考的国际象棋大师阿龙·尼姆佐维奇，用一个聪明的操场小故事来教学生。他说，想赢下对方一个虚弱的兵，并不需要直接去攻击它。你可以轻轻把它的保镖们引开，或者挡住他们的路，让他们再也帮不上忙。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: Long ago, a wise chess teacher named Aron Nimzowitsch noticed a quiet mistake that many new players made. Instead of helping all their pieces step out onto the board, they would chase after a single, lonely pawn. It is easy to get distracted by one small prize, but it leaves the rest of your army waiting in the shadows.
variants.luca: Aron Nimzowitsch saw that beginners love to charge straight into battle with wild energy! They zoom across the board to snatch up one tiny pawn, totally forgetting to set up their main army. This eager rush might feel exciting, but it actually ruins their plans before the real fight even starts.
variants.cn: 很久以前，睿智的棋艺老师阿龙·尼姆佐维奇发现，许多新手都会悄悄犯同一个错误。他们不去帮所有棋子一个个走上棋盘，反而追着一个孤零零的小兵满场跑。一个小小的“奖品”确实容易让人分心，可这样一来，你的大部队就只能躲在阴影里干等着啦。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

variants.lucy: Long ago, in a beautiful seaside town, a player named Aron faced a giant, stubborn pawn standing right in the middle of the board. Instead of just building a slow wall to block it, Aron quietly placed his pieces in perfect, waiting spots. With one gentle nudge of his own pawn, he swept the giant away and changed the whole game.
variants.luca: Aron wasn't going to sit back and play defense all day. He spent his time setting up a brilliant, secret trap, waiting for the perfect second to strike. Boom! He launched a single pawn forward, smashing the enemy's center to pieces and turning the whole battle around.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在一座美丽的海边小镇上，棋手阿龙遇到了一个又大又倔的兵，稳稳地站在棋盘正中央。阿龙没有慢吞吞地修一堵墙去堵它，而是悄悄把自己的棋子一个个摆到最完美的位置，静静等待。然后，他轻轻一推自己的小兵——那个“巨人”就被扫了出去，整盘棋一下子翻转过来。

source.author: Aron Nimzowitsch

stories.title: A Bad Move with the Wrong Name

variants.lucy: Long ago in the sixteenth century, a thoughtful writer named Damiano crafted a book to protect chess players from making a terrible mistake at the very start of the game. He carefully explained why this particular opening move would leave your pieces weak and unprotected. Yet, in a quiet twist of history, people began calling that exact, clumsy setup by his own name instead.
variants.luca: Imagine writing a brilliant guidebook to warn players away from a disastrous opening trap, only for the world to name the trap after you! That is the wild trick history played on a writer named Damiano back in the fifteen-hundreds. He loudly declared that this specific start was a terrible mistake, but today, players still call this awful defense by his name.
variants.cn: 很久以前的十六世纪，有位细心的作家叫达米亚诺。他写了一本书，想保护棋手们，别在开局的时候犯下一个可怕的错误。他认认真真地解释了，为什么这步开局棋会让你的棋子又虚弱又没人保护。可历史偏偏开了个安静的小玩笑——后来人们竟然就用他的名字，来称呼这个笨拙的下法。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: A Clever Trick to Reach the Prince
stories.titleCn: 把书送到王子手里的妙计

variants.lucy: Long ago in the year 1561, a Spanish priest named Ruy López wrote down his favorite chess secrets in a special book. He hoped a young prince who adored the game would get to read his quiet pages. To make sure the book found its way into the royal palace, he wrote a lovely dedication to the prince's own teacher.
variants.luca: Ruy López had a brilliant plan to get his new chess book to Spain's young prince! He knew the royal kid loved chess, but getting a book into a palace was a tough mission. So, he pulled a clever move and dedicated the book to the prince's personal teacher instead. That way, the teacher would definitely show the book to his royal student!
variants.cn: 很久以前，在1561年，一位名叫鲁伊·洛佩斯的西班牙神父，把自己最喜欢的国际象棋秘诀写进了一本特别的书里。他多希望那位热爱下棋的小王子，能读到这些安静的书页啊。为了让这本书顺利走进王宫，他想了个好主意——把书题献给王子的老师。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a gentle priest named Ruy Lopez watched a young prince named Charles play chess with quiet focus. The prince loved the wooden pieces and the clever squares so much that it touched the priest's heart. To share this joy, the priest sat down and wrote one of the very first guidebooks, filled with secrets to help everyone learn the game.
variants.luca: Imagine a real-life prince from the old days who was totally obsessed with conquering the chessboard! A priest named Ruy Lopez saw this royal battle-spirit and decided to do something legendary. He grabbed his quill and wrote down a master plan, creating one of the world's first-ever chess rulebooks to help future champions win their own matches.
variants.cn: 很久很久以前，在西班牙，有一位温和的神父，名叫鲁伊·洛佩斯。他注意到小王子卡洛斯下国际象棋时总是全神贯注。小王子那么喜欢那些木头棋子和巧妙的方格，这份热爱深深打动了神父的心。为了把这份快乐分享给更多人，神父坐下来，写出了世界上最早的国际象棋指南之一，里面装满了帮助大家学会下棋的小秘密。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: A Royal Guard for a Chess Book

variants.lucy: Hundreds of years ago, a thoughtful player named Ruy López wrote a special guide filled with chess secrets. The King of Spain wanted to protect these precious pages, so he signed a royal paper just for this book. This gentle guard of ink made sure that no one could copy the writer's hard work without permission.
variants.luca: Imagine having the King of Spain protect your chess strategies! He made a strict royal rule that absolutely nobody could copy Ruy's new book. Anyone who dared to break this law faced a giant penalty of twenty thousand coins. That would be worth a massive fortune today!
variants.cn: 几百年前，有一位爱动脑筋的棋手，名叫鲁伊·洛佩斯。他写了一本特别的指南，里面装满了国际象棋的秘密。西班牙国王想保护这些珍贵的书页，于是专门为这本书签下了一道皇家文书。这位用墨水写成的“温柔卫士”守在书前，保证谁也不能不经允许，就抄走作者辛辛苦苦写下的成果。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: A Royal Shield for Ruy Lopez
stories.titleCn: 鲁伊·洛佩斯的皇家盾牌

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a gentle priest named Ruy Lopez spent many quiet hours writing down his favorite chess secrets in a special book. To keep this treasure safe, the king himself promised that no one else could print the book for ten whole years. It was like a royal shield made of paper and ink, protecting the priest's hard work.
variants.luca: But watch out, because copying that book without permission was an incredibly dangerous move back then! King Philip the Second set up rules so fierce that thieves faced giant fines or even the ultimate punishment. It was a high-stakes adventure just to guard those chess pages from rivals.
variants.cn: 很久以前的西班牙，有一位温和的神父，名叫鲁伊·洛佩斯。他花了许许多多安静的时光，把自己最喜欢的国际象棋秘密写进一本特别的书里。为了保护这件宝贝，国王亲自许下承诺：整整十年里，谁也不许印这本书。这就像一面用纸和墨水做成的皇家盾牌，守护着神父辛勤的成果。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Nearly nine centuries ago, a wise scholar named Abraham sat down in Spain to write a beautiful poem. He painted a picture of a quiet battlefield made of dark and light squares. On this board, two armies meet, yet there is no clashing of metal or sound of shields. It is a silent, magical dance where only gentle ideas guide the pieces.
variants.luca: Imagine a massive clash where nobody gets hurt because the only weapons are inside your own mind! That is exactly what Abraham described in his epic poem nine hundred years ago. He saw the checkered board as a thrilling battleground for two rival armies. Every single move is a secret plan, proving that the ultimate power is just a brilliant strategy.
variants.cn: 差不多九百年前，在西班牙，有一位聪明的学者，名叫亚伯拉罕。他坐下来，写了一首美丽的诗。诗里描绘了一个安静的战场，由深色和浅色的方格拼成。在这块棋盘上，两支大军相遇了，却听不到刀剑相碰的声音，也没有盾牌的撞响。这是一场无声又神奇的舞蹈——指挥棋子的，只有轻轻的念头和巧妙的主意。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Long ago, in a famous old book, a character named Sancho Panza shared a beautiful secret about chess. He noticed that during a match, every carved figure has its own unique strength and a specific duty to perform. But as soon as the playtime ends, the majestic rulers and the humble helpers are all gently gathered into the very same storage pouch.
variants.luca: In a classic adventure tale, Sancho Panza described the ultimate end of a chess battle. While the clash is happening, some pieces hold massive authority while others have small tasks to complete. But the moment the fight finishes, the rules change completely. The grandest queens and the smallest soldiers get jumbled up and tossed right back into the exact same bag!
variants.cn: 很久以前，在一本有名的老书里，有个叫桑丘·潘萨的人物，说出了一个关于国际象棋的美妙秘密。他发现，下棋的时候，每一枚雕刻的棋子都有自己独特的本领，要完成自己特别的任务。可是棋局一结束，威风的王和后，还有那些默默帮忙的小兵，都会被轻轻地收进同一个袋子里。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Five centuries ago, chess writers shared unusual secrets that had nothing to do with the wooden pieces. They suggested placing the table so the morning sunlight would beam straight into the other player's eyes. If the game took place after dusk, they recommended setting a dancing flame to the right of your challenger to cast confusing shapes across the squares.
variants.luca: Back in the fifteen-hundreds, masters used wild tactics that weren't even on the board! One old guidebook told players to angle the seat so the blazing sun would beam right into their rival's face. During evening matches, they would position a wavering candle on the right to mess with the enemy using spooky, shifting shapes.
variants.cn: 五百年前，写棋书的人分享过一些奇奇怪怪的秘诀，跟木头棋子一点关系都没有。他们建议把桌子摆好位置，让清晨的阳光正好直直地照进对手的眼睛。要是天黑以后下棋，他们还建议在对手右边放一支跳动的蜡烛，让摇晃的影子在棋盘的方格上晃来晃去，把对手看得晕头转向。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: How the Gambit Got Its Name

variants.lucy: Long ago, a writer named Ruy López wrote down a beautiful new word for a clever way to play. He borrowed the term "gambit" from the Italian language to describe a quiet trap. By offering a small piece as a gift, a player could lure their opponent into a surprise.
variants.luca: This was a daring plan built for speed and surprise! Ruy used these clever sacrifices to challenge the older masters who were used to a much slower game. His lightning-fast tricks caught them completely off guard, changing how the game was played forever.
variants.cn: 很久以前，有位作家叫鲁伊·洛佩斯，他为一种聪明的下法写下了一个漂亮的新词。他从意大利语里借来“弃兵局”这个词，用来形容一个安安静静的陷阱：棋手故意把一枚小棋子当礼物送出去，引着对手一步一步走进意想不到的圈套。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: How the Queen Became the Strongest Piece
stories.titleCn: 后是怎么变成最强棋子的

variants.lucy: Once, the chess queen was very quiet and could only step one tiny square at a time. But in Spain, a real queen named Isabella wore armor and guided her armies with great care. The people wanted their game to mirror her strength, so they gave the wooden queen the power to glide all the way across the board.
variants.luca: Imagine a queen who could only crawl one space at a time—so boring! Then came Queen Isabella of Spain, a fierce leader who actually marched right into battle with her soldiers. Chess players saw her bravery and decided the game needed a major upgrade. They unlocked her ultimate move, letting her charge across the entire battlefield in a single swoop!
variants.cn: 从前，棋盘上的后特别安静，每次只能小心翼翼地挪一格。可是在西班牙，有一位真正的女王，名叫伊莎贝拉。她穿上铠甲，细心地指挥着自己的军队。人们希望棋盘上的后也能像她一样强大，于是就送给木头做的后一种新本领——让她可以一口气滑过整张棋盘。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: Is Chess a City or a Battlefield?
stories.titleCn: 国际象棋是城市还是战场？

variants.lucy: A monk named Jacobus looked at the wooden board and saw a quiet, busy town. He imagined the little pieces as neighbors, like bakers and builders, all helping each other live in peace. To him, every square was a tiny street where people worked side by side.
variants.luca: But then a Spanish champion named Ruy Lopez charged in with a totally different plan! He declared that those sixty-four squares were actually a wild, daring battlefield. For him, the game was a thrilling clash between two noble forces fighting for victory.
variants.cn: 有一位修士叫雅各布斯，他看着木头棋盘，看到的却是一座安静又热闹的小城。在他的想象里，小小的棋子就像住在一起的邻居——有面包师，有建筑工，大家互相帮忙，和和气气地过日子。在他眼里，每一个方格都是一条小小的街道，人们在那里肩并肩地干活。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: Ruy López and the Poisonous Snakes

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a gentle priest named Ruy López spent many quiet hours writing down his favorite chess secrets. But he worried that other players might be unkind about his work, comparing their harsh words to hidden, biting serpents. To keep his mind at peace, he asked a very important nobleman to protect his beautiful book.
variants.luca: Ruy López was stepping into a real battle zone when he published his chess ideas! He actually warned his readers that jealous rivals were like venomous snakes waiting to strike from the grass. So, he made a clever defensive move by putting a mighty nobleman's name on the front page as a shield.
variants.cn: 很久以前的西班牙，温和的神父鲁伊·洛佩斯花了许多安静的时光，把自己最喜欢的国际象棋秘密一点一点写下来。可他担心别的棋手会说他的坏话，还把那些刻薄的话比作藏在暗处、随时会咬人的毒蛇。为了让自己安心，他请了一位非常重要的贵族大人，来保护他这本美丽的书。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: Sneaky Tricks from a Chess Priest

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a quiet priest named Ruy López discovered that winning chess games was about more than just moving the wooden pieces. He noticed how easily a player could lose focus if the bright afternoon glare got in their way. He gently suggested placing the board so the daylight became your quiet helper.
variants.luca: But that was not his only wild plan for victory! He also told players to challenge opponents who were already exhausted and yawning. To guarantee a win, he even suggested using strange, unfamiliar pieces that would totally confuse the other side.
variants.cn: 很久以前的西班牙，安静的神父鲁伊·洛佩斯发现，想赢下一盘国际象棋，可不只是会挪动木头棋子那么简单。他注意到，要是午后刺眼的阳光晃到眼睛，棋手很容易就走神了。于是他悄悄建议：摆棋盘的时候选好方向，让阳光变成你这边不出声的小帮手。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: The Birth of the Ruy Lopez
stories.titleCn: 鲁伊·洛佩斯开局的诞生

variants.lucy: Long ago in the sixteenth century, a thoughtful Spanish priest sat quietly by his wooden board. He realized that the usual way of starting a game left a tiny weakness that others missed. By gently sliding his bishop to a new square called b5, he created a clever plan that players still love to use today.
variants.luca: This clever priest decided to shake up the chess world with a surprise attack! Instead of playing it safe in the middle, he launched his bishop way forward to create instant trouble for his opponent. This bold move was so successful that it became one of the most legendary battle plans in history.
variants.cn: 很久以前的十六世纪，一位爱思考的西班牙神父静静地坐在木棋盘前。他发现，大家平时习惯的开局方法里，藏着一个别人都没注意到的小弱点。他轻轻地把象滑到一个叫 b5 的新格子上，创造出一个聪明的计划——直到今天，棋手们还是特别喜欢用这一招呢。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Over five hundred years ago in Portugal, a quiet apothecary named Pedro Damiano spent his time writing down the secrets of the board. He wanted to help anyone learn how to guide their pieces gracefully. His wonderful book became so popular that workshops printed it over and over again for families to treasure.
variants.luca: Imagine mixing medicine by day and plotting epic chess victories by night! This Portuguese pharmacist wrote a strategy guide that became one of the first smash-hit books in history. Everyone wanted a piece of his clever tactics, so printers had to crank out version after version to keep up with the demand.
variants.cn: 五百多年前的葡萄牙，有一位安静的药剂师，名叫佩德罗·达米亚诺。他把棋盘上的秘密一条一条写下来，希望帮助每一个人学会优雅地指挥自己的棋子。他这本好书后来大受欢迎，印书坊一遍又一遍地加印，好让一家又一家的人把它当成宝贝珍藏起来。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Five hundred years ago, a quiet priest named Ruy López packed his bags for a long journey to Rome. While visiting on church duties, he sat down at wooden tables to play the local masters. With gentle patience, he won every single game he played. Though the title did not exist yet, we now look back at him as the world's very first champion.
variants.luca: A priest named Ruy López marched into Italy five centuries ago and decided to take on the strongest players he could find. He swept through Rome, crushing the local masters with his bold strategies. He made every tough victory look totally effortless. History books now celebrate this brave traveler as the planet's very first chess king.
variants.cn: 五百年前，安静的神父鲁伊·洛佩斯收拾好行李，踏上了去罗马的漫长旅程。在那里办教会事务的空闲时间，他坐到木桌前，和当地的高手们下国际象棋。他不急不躁，温和又有耐心，结果每一盘棋都赢了。虽然那时还没有“世界冠军”这个头衔，但现在回头看，大家都把他当作世界上第一位国际象棋冠军。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Long ago in the year 1616, a gentle German duke named Augustus worked on a special book about chess.
