He translated the wise words so everyone could read them, but he did not want his royal title on the cover. Instead, he chose a beautiful secret name, Gustavus Selenus, to sign his lovely pages.
variants.luca: Imagine a powerful ruler sneaking around to write a book! Duke Augustus wanted to share a legendary chess guide, but he needed a brilliant disguise. He cooked up a secret identity, Gustavus Selenus, and slipped it onto the cover like a spy on a mission.
variants.cn: 很久以前的 1616 年，德国有一位温和的公爵，名叫奥古斯特。他在忙一本关于国际象棋的特别的书：他把书里充满智慧的文字翻译出来，好让每个人都能读懂。可是他不想把自己的贵族头衔印在封面上，于是挑了一个好听的秘密名字——古斯塔夫斯·塞勒努斯，签在了那些可爱的书页上。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: The First Modern Chess Game was a Love Poem
stories.titleCn: 第一盘现代国际象棋是一首爱情诗

variants.lucy: Over five hundred years ago in Spain, three poets decided to write a beautiful story about the very first modern chess game. They turned the board into a quiet battlefield of love between two ancient Roman gods. One poet played as Mars, moving his pawn forward, while another played as Venus to defend her side. Their third friend watched over them, gently explaining the brand-new rules of the game.
variants.luca: Picture a chess match so exciting that three writers turned it into an epic clash of the gods! Mars charged his king's pawn forward two whole steps to start the attack. Venus immediately blocked his path with a clever counter-move of her own queen's pawn. To keep the peace, a third poet acted as the referee, calling out the brand-new rules of this updated game.
variants.cn: 五百多年前的西班牙，三位诗人决定写一个美丽的故事，讲的是世界上第一盘现代国际象棋。他们把棋盘变成了一个安安静静的战场，对阵的双方是两位古罗马的神。一位诗人扮演战神玛尔斯，把兵向前推进；另一位扮演爱神维纳斯，守住自己这一边。他们的第三位朋友则在旁边看着，温和地讲解这套全新的下棋规则。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Over four hundred years ago, a priest from Spain named Ruy López sat down to write a book filled with his quiet chess secrets. Eager players in Italy and France quickly translated the pages so they could try his clever ideas themselves. It took hundreds of years, however, for the entire guide to finally be printed in English.
variants.luca: Imagine a guide so packed with brilliant strategies that players across Europe scrambled to get their hands on it! To learn his winning style, rivals rushed to translate the pages into French and Italian. This grand chess adventure lasted for centuries before the complete book was finally printed in English!
variants.cn: 四百多年前，西班牙的神父鲁伊·洛佩斯坐下来，写了一本装满他国际象棋小秘密的书。意大利和法国那些迫不及待的棋手们，很快就把书页翻译成自己的语言，好亲自试一试他的聪明点子。不过，要等上好几百年，这本指南的全部内容才终于用英语印了出来。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Way back in the late fifteenth century, a Spanish author named Luis de Lucena sat down with ink and parchment to record the new rules of chess. Inside his precious book, he drew a quiet trap where a single knight completely surrounds the opposing king. Sadly, as the years drifted by, people forgot his name and gave the honor to a different player named Philidor instead.
variants.luca: Imagine pulling off a sneaky knight strike, only for someone else to steal your glory centuries later! That is exactly what happened to Luis, who mapped out this epic battle plan way back in his 1497 handbook. A player named Philidor got his name on the trophy, but Luis was the true mastermind behind the trap.
variants.cn: 早在十五世纪快结束的时候，西班牙作家路易斯·德·卢塞纳拿起墨水和羊皮纸，坐下来记录国际象棋的新规则。在他那本珍贵的书里，他画下了一个安静的陷阱：只用一个马，就把对方的王困得死死的。可惜呀，随着岁月慢慢流走，人们忘记了他的名字，把这份荣誉给了另一位棋手——菲利多尔。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Imagine a quiet stone room in Spain where a king sat playing his favorite game. Suddenly, a guard rushed in because a captive in the dungeon needed to share a final secret before it was too late. Since no holy man could be found in the castle, the king looked at his clever opponent. He gently declared that his chess partner was now a real-life priest so the duty could be finished.
variants.luca: Talk about a crazy emergency! The king absolutely had to find a church leader to hear a captive's final confession, but the castle was totally empty. He looked down at the board, got a wild idea, and pointed his finger right at his chess opponent. Just like that, with one quick royal command, a regular player was drafted into the priesthood to save the day!
variants.cn: 想象一下，在西班牙一间安静的石头屋子里，国王正坐着下他最喜欢的国际象棋。忽然，一名卫兵急匆匆地跑进来——地牢里有个囚犯，想趁还来得及，说出最后的秘密。可是整座城堡里找不到一位神职人员。国王看了看对面这位聪明的棋友，温和地宣布：从这一刻起，他的下棋伙伴就是一位真正的神父啦！这样，这件要紧的事就能办成了。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: The Italian Pawn Escape
stories.titleCn: 意大利小兵的逃脱妙计

variants.lucy: Long ago in the sunny valleys of Italy, chess was played with a gentle touch of wonder. A tiny pawn could glide forward two whole spaces, safely slipping past an enemy waiting right next to it. They called this quiet escape the passing battle, and it kept the little soldiers safe on their journey.
variants.luca: Imagine sprinting right through enemy lines without getting caught! Five hundred years ago, Italian players used a special rule where pawns could leap two squares to dodge a sideways ambush. This daring move was called the passing battle, and it turned their games into a fast-paced rescue mission.
variants.cn: 很久很久以前，在阳光洒满山谷的意大利，人们下国际象棋的方式带着一点奇妙的温柔。一个小小的兵可以一口气向前滑两格，安安稳稳地从旁边正等着抓它的敌人身边溜过去。人们把这种悄悄的逃脱叫作“过路之战”，它让小兵们在旅途中平平安安。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: In the year 1575, the King of Spain invited the world's finest players to a grand palace tournament. A quiet player named Leonardo won the final games, receiving a beautiful cape made of soft fur and heavy sacks of gold coins. Instead of keeping all the wealth for himself, he made a gentle request to the king. He asked that his entire home village be freed from paying taxes for twenty long years, bringing comfort to his neighbors.
variants.luca: Imagine a massive chess showdown in a royal castle, where the ultimate champion would take home a legendary treasure. A bold player named Leonardo defeated everyone to win the grand prize of gold and a fancy royal cloak. But his greatest move happened after the game ended. He used his victory to strike a deal with the king, saving his hometown from taxes for two whole decades!
variants.cn: 公元1575年，西班牙国王把全世界最厉害的棋手请进了富丽堂皇的宫殿，举办了一场盛大的比赛。一位安静的棋手莱昂纳多赢下了最后的对局，得到了一件柔软的毛皮披风，还有一袋袋沉甸甸的金币。可他没有把财富都留给自己，而是轻轻地向国王提了一个请求：让他的家乡整整二十年都不用交税。乡亲们听了，心里别提多暖和了。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: The King Who Preferred Brains Over Luck
stories.titleCn: 爱动脑筋、不爱碰运气的国王

variants.lucy: Long ago in ancient India, a gentle ruler named King Balhait watched his court toss dice and felt something was missing. He wished for a game where a person's own thoughtful choices decided the path to victory. To show his people a better way, he shared the quiet beauty of chess, comparing the carved figures to the glowing stars in the night sky.
variants.luca: King Balhait was totally done with letting random dice rolls decide who won! He wanted a real clash of minds where clever planning and bold moves ruled the day. He used the chessboard to map out daring army strategies, proving that smart thinking always beats lucky guesses.
variants.cn: 很久很久以前，在古老的印度，有一位温和的国王，名叫巴勒海特。他看着宫廷里的人们掷骰子玩游戏，总觉得少了点什么。他盼望有一种游戏，输赢是靠自己用心思考来决定的。于是，他把国际象棋安安静静的美分享给了大家，还把那些精雕细刻的棋子，比作夜空里一闪一闪的星星。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: The King Who Wrote the Book on Chess
stories.titleCn: 为国际象棋写书的国王

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a gentle king named Alfonso decided to capture the joy of games in a giant book. He asked artists to paint lovely, colorful pictures of people sitting quietly and playing chess. This beautiful creation traveled across Europe, helping people learn how to think deeply and plan their next steps.
variants.luca: King Alfonso of Spain loved a good challenge, so he gathered his scribes to make the ultimate game guide. It was packed with awesome, hand-drawn scenes of players facing off over the board. This massive project spread everywhere, training people to think like brilliant strategists.
variants.cn: 很久以前，西班牙有一位温和的国王，名叫阿方索。他决定把游戏带来的快乐统统装进一本大大的书里。他请画师们画出一幅幅漂亮的彩色图画，画里的人安安静静地坐着下国际象棋。这本美丽的书后来走遍了欧洲，帮助人们学会深深地思考，想好下一步该怎么走。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a thoughtful writer named Lucena printed one of the very first books about our favorite game. Today, players still practice a clever endgame trick named in his honor. But if you turn the dusty, yellowed pages of his ancient book, you will find that this special setup is completely missing.
variants.luca: Imagine a secret code named after a master who never actually wrote it down! We all learn this brilliant winning setup and use his name to describe it. Yet, if you hunt through his original guidebook from five hundred years ago, the secret formula is totally gone.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，有一位爱思考的作家，名叫卢塞纳。他印出了关于我们最爱的国际象棋的最早的书之一。直到今天，棋手们还在练习一个用他的名字命名的聪明的残局妙招。可是呢，如果你翻开他那本落满灰尘、纸页发黄的老书，你会发现——这个特别的棋局竟然根本不在里面！

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Imagine holding a delicate, hand-written book that is over five hundred years old. Its pages whisper secrets about how to move the chess pieces in brand new ways. Some people believe a teacher crafted this guide especially for a young prince in Spain.
variants.luca: This was the ultimate secret handbook of its time, packed with clever plans! We still do not know if it was written in Portugal or made for a royal Spanish family. The author left no name, leaving us with a brilliant chess mystery that nobody has solved yet.
variants.cn: 想象一下，你手里捧着一本五百多岁、薄薄的手写小书。它的书页轻声细语，讲着用全新方法移动棋子的秘密。有人相信，这本小书是一位老师特意为西班牙的一位小王子写的呢。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Long ago in the fifteen-hundreds, a priest in Spain named Ruy Lopez spent his quiet hours writing a book about chess. He wanted to help players by pointing out the errors of a past champion named Damiano. In his writing, he explained a wonderful word we still use today called the gambit. It originally came from an old Italian wrestling trick where you sweep your opponent's ankle.
variants.luca: Imagine a clever priest named Ruy Lopez challenging the old ideas of an older player named Damiano. In his action-packed book, Lopez revealed a sneaky move called the gambit. This word actually comes from Italian athletes who loved to trip their rival's leg to win a match. It is the ultimate surprise attack!
variants.cn: 在很久以前的十六世纪，西班牙有一位神父，名叫鲁伊·洛佩斯。他喜欢在安静的时光里写一本关于国际象棋的书。他想帮助棋手们，就把从前一位高手达米亚诺书里的错误一一指了出来。在书里，他还讲了一个我们今天还在用的奇妙的词——“弃兵局”。这个词原本来自意大利古老的摔跤招式，意思是伸腿一勾，把对手绊个趔趄！

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: The Priest Who Defended Chess Books

variants.lucy: A long time ago, people thought it was impossible to write a guide for chess because the game has endless paths. A Spanish priest named Ruy López disagreed, believing that a player's mind is like a quiet, empty field. Just as a farmer cares for the soil to help crops grow, he believed we must study to prepare our minds for any surprise.
variants.luca: Imagine being told that chess has too many wild moves to ever write down in a guide! That is what people believed in the 1500s, but a brave priest named Ruy López refused to back down. He argued that you have to prepare your mind like a farmer works the land, getting it ready for action. By studying hard, you can stand strong against any unexpected move your opponent throws at you!
variants.cn: 很久以前，人们觉得国际象棋根本没法写成指南，因为棋盘上的路千千万万，数也数不清。可西班牙神父鲁伊·洛佩斯不同意。他相信，棋手的头脑就像一片安静的空田地。就像农夫细心耕耘土壤，庄稼才能长大一样，他相信我们也要好好学习，让头脑做好准备，迎接棋盘上的任何意外。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: The Priest with the Golden Rook

variants.lucy: Deep inside a quiet Spanish palace, King Philip spent his days studying the chess board. He found a wonderful partner in a priest named Ruy Lopez, who played with great patience and care. To thank his friend, the king placed a beautiful golden chain around the priest's neck. Hanging from the links was a tiny, polished rook that caught the soft candlelight.
variants.luca: King Philip of Spain was absolutely wild about chess, and he wanted the cleverest player in the land to help him run the kingdom. That champion was a priest named Ruy Lopez, who defeated everyone with his brilliant moves. To celebrate these victories, the king gave him an awesome treasure to wear. It was a heavy golden chain featuring a miniature, sparkling rook as the ultimate trophy.
variants.cn: 在西班牙一座安静的宫殿深处，国王费利佩天天对着棋盘琢磨。他找到了一位特别棒的对弈伙伴——神父鲁伊·洛佩斯，他下棋既耐心又细心。为了感谢这位朋友，国王把一条漂亮的金链子戴在了神父的脖子上。链子上挂着一个小小的、擦得亮亮的车，在柔柔的烛光里一闪一闪。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

variants.lucy: Hundreds of years ago, a Spanish player named Ruy Lopez looked closely at a chess book written by a man named Damiano. Ruy thought the pages were so full of errors that the author must have been dreaming instead of thinking. But the little book had its own quiet strength, traveling across borders and being translated into many different languages.
variants.luca: Ruy Lopez launched a giant attack with his words, teasing that Damiano fell fast asleep at his desk while writing his chess guide! He claimed the book was packed with silly blunders from cover to cover. But Damiano got the last laugh because his book became an absolute blockbuster worldwide!
variants.cn: 几百年前，西班牙棋手鲁伊·洛佩斯仔仔细细地读了一本棋书，作者名叫达米亚诺。鲁伊觉得书里的错误实在太多了，心想作者写书的时候八成不是在思考，而是在做梦吧！可这本小书自有它安安静静的力量——它跨过一个又一个国家，被翻译成了好多好多种语言。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: The Slow Battles of Ancient Chess
stories.titleCn: 古代象棋的慢悠悠大战

variants.lucy: Long ago, chess began as a very quiet, patient game. Players spent their first ten turns gently arranging their pieces, making sure every wooden soldier was in its perfect spot. No one rushed across the middle of the board until both sides were completely prepared.
variants.luca: Imagine a giant battle where you had to wait ten whole turns before you could even launch an attack! Both armies stayed on their own territory, preparing their secret formations. Only when the preparation was complete did the soldiers finally march across the border for a massive clash!
variants.cn: 很久很久以前，国际象棋刚出现的时候，是一种特别安静、特别有耐心的游戏。棋手们要花上整整十个回合，轻轻地摆好自己的棋子，让每一个小木头士兵都站在最合适的位置上。在双方都完完全全准备好之前，谁也不会急着冲过棋盘的中线。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: Writing a Book Out of Anger

variants.lucy: Five hundred years ago, a gentle priest from Spain named Ruy López sat down to read a new chess scroll. As he turned the pages, he noticed that the advice was filled with quiet errors that would confuse players. He decided to carefully pen his own instructions to show the true, correct paths across the board, creating a work that became one of the most celebrated handbooks ever written.
variants.luca: Imagine reading a chess rulebook so bad that it makes you want to shout! That is exactly what happened to Ruy López, who got so fired up by another writer's blunders that he launched a literary rescue mission. He immediately penned his own master plan to defeat those errors, creating a legendary playbook that changed the game forever.
variants.cn: 五百年前，西班牙有一位温和的神父，名叫鲁伊·洛佩斯。他坐下来读一卷新出的棋书，可是一页一页翻下去，他发现里面悄悄藏着好多错误，会把棋手们带糊涂的。于是他决定认认真真地写下自己的讲解，告诉大家棋盘上真正正确的路该怎么走。没想到，这本书后来成了历史上最有名的棋类手册之一！

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

stories.title: Writing Chess Books Out of Anger

variants.lucy: Long ago, a thoughtful chess player named Ruy López noticed that an older book was full of mistakes. He gently picked up his quill to write down the true beauty of the game, guiding players with much better care. Hundreds of years later, another quiet master did the very same thing to protect his students from bad advice.
variants.luca: Imagine getting so mad at a terrible chess book that you write your own just to prove them wrong! That is exactly how Ruy López started his legendary battle of the books back in the fifteen-hundreds. Later on, a grandmaster named Richard Réti launched his own literary rescue mission because he couldn't stand seeing awful tips in print!
variants.cn: 很久以前，一位爱思考的棋手鲁伊·洛佩斯发现，一本老棋书里全是错误。他轻轻拿起羽毛笔，写下这盘棋真正的美，用更细心的方式指引棋手们。几百年后，另一位安静的大师也做了一模一样的事——就为了不让坏建议害了他的学生们。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath
